paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this passage. Before one trumpet sounds, heaven goes quiet, and then the prayers of the saints go up before God from an angel's hand, with the incense (Revelation 8:1, 3-4). Those prayers don't fade away. They rise up before God, and what comes next on the earth comes after that. So when you pray and it feels like nobody's listening, remember who is.

Then come the trumpets, and I'll be honest, the fire, the sea, the star and the dark are HEAVY. A third of the earth is burned up, a third of the sea turns to blood, and many people die from the bitter waters (Revelation 8:7-11). I think this part hurts, and it should. But notice it comes in measures, a third at a time, and it comes with a warning, because the eagle cries, "Woe! Woe! Woe to those who dwell on the earth…" (Revelation 8:13). Warnings matter, friend, and this one is loud.

So what do you do with it? You stay ready, the same way my ovens stay ready. Three trumpets are still to come, so this story isn't over (Revelation 8:13). No one knows the day or the hour, not even the Son, only the Father (Matthew 24:36), so no guessing from me. Keep praying, keep your apron on, and keep your eyes on the Lamb who opened that seal.
